question: Under the AMLR, do the PEP enhanced measures also extend to a politician's spouse or close business partner?
evidence_note: AMLR Art. 46 (p.73): measures of Arts 42, 44, 45 also apply to family members and close associates.

question: Does the 4th AML Directive allow Member States to exempt low-value prepaid e-money cards from customer due diligence?
evidence_note: AMLD Art. 12 (pp.19-20): e-money exemption, EUR 250 limits.

question: What should a bank do with an incoming cross-border wire that is missing the originator's details, per FATF Recommendation 16?
evidence_note: R.16 text (p.18) + INR 16 paras 27-31 on intermediary/beneficiary institutions (p.86).

question: EBA/GL/2022/15: what happens if the selfie video taken during remote onboarding is too blurry to recognise the customer?
evidence_note: Para 24(b)-(c) (p.16): sufficient quality, stop the process on technical shortcomings; verification clarity/quality (pp.19-20).

question: How many years after a client relationship ends do we have to keep the KYC file under Directive 2015/849?
evidence_note: AMLD Art. 40 (p.29): five years after the end of the business relationship.

question: The 2015/849 Directive requires enhanced due diligence on PEPs - what transaction red flags should make us suspicious about a PEP client?
evidence_note: Named: AMLD. Answer: FATF PEP guidance Annex 1 red flags (pp.29-33); AMLD has no red-flag list.

question: Before we close accounts under the AMLR because a whole customer group is high risk, what alternatives does the EBA expect us to consider first?
evidence_note: Named: AMLR (+EBA). Answer: EBA/GL/2023/04 paras 10-12 (pp.10-11): no blanket de-risking, consider mitigating measures first.

question: Under FATF Recommendation 10, how should a bank run a liveness check when customers verify their identity with a selfie in an app?
evidence_note: Named: FATF R.10. Answer: EBA remote onboarding GL 4.4 (p.19): liveness detection. R.10 says nothing on liveness.

question: Article 18 of Directive 2015/849 requires EDD - what specific EDD steps are expected for high-net-worth private banking clients?
evidence_note: Named: AMLD Art. 18. Answer: EBA risk factor GL, Guideline 12 wealth management, EDD measures (pp.79-80).

question: FATF Recommendation 12 covers PEPs - how long after leaving office should a former minister still be treated as a PEP?
evidence_note: Named: FATF R.12. Answer: FATF PEP guidance 'Time limits of PEP status' (p.14, risk-based, no fixed limit); EU rule AMLR Art. 45 (p.72, at least 12 months).

question: What does the FATF say about relying on commercial PEP screening databases?
evidence_note: FATF PEP guidance section D 'Commercial databases' (pp.17-18).

question: According to the EBA, can a bank accept an expired passport from an asylum seeker who has no other ID?
evidence_note: EBA/GL/2023/04 para 19(a)-(b) (pp.12-13): alternative documentation incl. expired identity documents where national law permits.

question: Does the EBA set an ownership percentage threshold for identifying a company's beneficial owner?
evidence_note: Authority mismatch: the 25% threshold is in AMLD Art. 3(6) (p.14) and AMLR Art. 52 (p.75); EBA GL discuss BO identification (pp.27-28) without a threshold.

question: Can we onboard a new customer entirely over a video call, without them ever visiting a branch?
evidence_note: Remote onboarding verification (pp.19-20); EBA risk factors: non-face-to-face delivery channel (p.22) and guidelines 4.29-4.31 (pp.30-31).

question: If we can't confirm who really owns a corporate client, do we have to drop them?
evidence_note: Inability to complete CDD incl. BO: AMLR Art. 21 (p.56), AMLD Art. 14(4) (p.21), FATF R.10 (p.16).
